text:
Alex Chen: Hey team, ACME Ops reporting lots of 429s this morning despite being on Dedicated capacity. They say throughput dropped to ~60% of their committed. Can we triage?
Maya Patel: marked. Alex, can you paste the request headers they get when 429 occurs (X-RateLimit-*, any pool identifiers)?
ACME Ops: here are headers from a failing request: 
`x-rw-rate-limit-id: pool_42_us-west`
`x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0`
`x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 15`
`x-rw-dedicated-pool: true`
`x-rw-request-latency-ms: 1200`
Alex Chen: They also attached service logs showing a flurry of 503s from the upstream GPU nodes right before the 429s. Attaching snippet: 
```
2026-02-25T09:12:17Z [pool_42] node-7 kernel: nvml: memory spike -> queued
2026-02-25T09:12:18Z [pool_42] router: route to fallback-model-v2
2026-02-25T09:12:19Z [pool_42] limiter: burst_credit exhausted -> returning 429
```
Maya Patel: Interesting — looks like node instability triggered fallback which then hit a stricter rate shape on the fallback variant. Is their traffic bursty? Any recent client-side rollout?
ACME Ops: We did a client rollout yesterday that batches some requests very tightly (200 qps bursts for ~30s).
Sara Ortiz: That lines up. Dedicated pools have two levers: the committed throughput (guaranteed) and burst credits (temporary). If nodes drop, the controller can temporarily reduce available burst to keep latency SLOs.
Jordan Kim: Quick sanity checks: 1) which model version were they pinned to in the Console? 2) are they using per-route rate-limiting keys or the account-level key? 3) what does the Console show for pool utilization and node health in that timeframe?
Alex Chen: Answers: they were pinned to model-q3 (pinned at api/v1/pinned/model-q3). They use a single API key shared across their services. Console screenshot attached shows pool utilization hitting 95% with two node reboots at 09:12.
Maya Patel: OK. Probable sequence: node flaps -> automatic reroute to fallback/model variant -> fallback has lower parallelism or lower burst config -> burst credits depleted -> API returns 429 with x-rw-rate-limit-remaining:0.
ACME Ops: Is that intended? They paid for committed capacity — shouldn't we preserve their SLA during node issues?
Sara Ortiz: Good question. SLA is about availability and average throughput under normal conditions. During hardware failures, the system attempts graceful degradation and uses routing policies to avoid violating latency SLOs for other tenants. Committed capacity tries to reserve a baseline, but if a node fails and the pool cannot rebuild capacity within the shaping window, the controller may apply strict shaping to avoid high queue times.
Jordan Kim: We should check their dedicated_throughput_cap setting and the pool's `burst_window_seconds` and `burst_token_size`. Those live in the Pool config in Console -> Dedicated -> Pools -> pool_42 -> Advanced.
Maya Patel: Actionable repro steps for eng-runtime: 1) Simulate a node drop in a test pool with similar config; 2) Replay ACME's burst pattern (200 qps x 30s) pinned to the same model variant; 3) capture router + limiter logs and X-RateLimit headers. Use this script: 
```
# simulate burst
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"ping"}' &
done
sleep 30
```
Alex Chen: I'm going to run that against a staging pool with identical config and will forward results.
Billing Bot: FYI: ACME's committed throughput is 180 qps (monthly contract). They used ~1.4x of that for 2 hours during the rollout — overage billing triggered but currently under grace because they opened a support case.
ACME Ops: If we increase burst credits will that avoid 429s? We're open to short-term adjustments.
Sara Ortiz: Increasing burst credits will help absorb spikes BUT it assumes underlying nodes can handle the extra concurrent work. If the spike coincides with node failures, you may just cause longer queues and higher latencies. Better approach: client-side smoothing + server-side steady shaping + scale up reserved capacity in Dedicated.
Maya Patel: Suggested immediate mitigations: 1) Client: add token-bucket limiter with max_burst=50 and sustained_rate=180 qps. 2) We can temporarily increase pool burst_token_size by 30% for 1 hour from Console (ops change). 3) Eng-runtime to verify fallback model parallelism and consider enabling soft-fallback with gradual ramp rather than hard cutover.
Jordan Kim: From engineering: we should also expose `x-rw-burst-credit` and `x-rw-pool-state` more clearly so clients see remaining burst budget. File a low-priority API telemetry enhancement ticket.
Alex Chen: I ran the staging replay and saw the same pattern: when a node was cycled, requests moved to fallback and we saw `x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0` within 12s of the event. Logs: 
```
router: reroute to fallback-model-v2 (parallelism=4)
limiter: new_per_client_quota=180 sustained / burst=60
limiter: client_key=acme_key remaining=0 reset_in=14
```
Sara Ortiz: Given logs, I recommend: - Short term: increase pool burst_token_size by 30% and advise ACME to throttle client bursts. - Mid term: add soft-fallback ramping and increase fallback model parallelism. - Long term: discuss committed capacity uplift on next invoice.
ACME Ops: Please do the short term change. If we still see 429s we'll consider increasing committed capacity. Also, can you confirm no auth/billing misconfig caused this?
Maya Patel: Confirmed: auth tokens valid; billing shows overage flagged but no billing-account block. This is strictly rate shaping due to pool state.
Billing Bot: I've added a note to the billing case (case# 2026-ACME-77) to waive overage in this window if we find system-level issues.
Jordan Kim: I'll pick up an engineering ticket to add better headers and an internal alert when fallback routing reduces burst budget. Tagging @Sara Ortiz and @Maya Patel.
Alex Chen: Thanks — ACME is standing by. I'll apply the temporary burst bump and reply with results in 15 minutes.
ACME Ops: thanks team :thumbsup:
Maya Patel: Follow-ups: - Alex, paste post-change sampling of headers in this thread. - Jordan, ETA on telemetry header ticket?
Jordan Kim: ETA 2 weeks for header telemetry PR, 1 week for internal alert rule.
Alex Chen: Post-change snapshot: 
`x-rw-burst-credit: 85`
`x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 42`
No 429s in the last 12 minutes during another small rollout.
ACME Ops: Looks stable so far. Appreciate the quick assist.
Maya Patel: Closing provisional triage. Will reopen if 429s reappear.\n[thread closed by Maya Patel]
